messages:
maya (Sales): Procurement at CareNimbus returned the OF with two hard asks: DocuSign ID Check for all signers, and a 99.9% uptime SLA with credits up to 15% monthly. This is a 3-month Dedicated POC ~ $49k. Need legal/eng/finance input.

devin (Legal): Please paste the exact procurement wording. High-level: notarization or large credit caps are risky for short POCs. We typically limit POC SLAs to 99.5% and cap credits to POC fees.

maya (Sales): Quote from their email: "Provider must enable identity verification via DocuSign for every signatory. Provider guarantees 99.9% availability; credits accrue per 0.1% below target up to 15% of monthly fees." They also added: "Provider shall accept notarized signature on request for contracts > $200k."

sam (Solutions): Tech-wise we can turn on DocuSign ID Check for the envelope. The mini dedicated pool can be provisioned in ~4 business days. But committing 99.9% for tiny pools is risky due to variability.

hira (Engineering): Agreed. Our standard Dedicated SLA in contracts is 99.5% with standard credits. For POCs we prefer 99.5% and a credit cap equal to the fees paid. Also recommend clarifying measurement window (rolling 30-day) and exclusions (scheduled maintenance, customer-caused outages).

devin (Legal): Proposed counter language: "For Proof-of-Concepts, Provider offers a 99.5% uptime SLA. Service credits for POCs are limited to the aggregate fees paid for the POC term. Provider accepts electronic signatures executed via DocuSign; DocuSign's identity verification satisfies Provider's signer authentication requirements. Provider is not liable for third-party verification failures. Notarization requests for contracts under $250,000 are subject to escalation and not required for POCs." Any objections?

frank (Finance): Finance is comfortable capping credits to POC fees. If Sales needs negotiation ammo we can offer a one-time conversion credit equal to 7.5% of the POC fees if customer signs an annual Dedicated commitment within 60 days of POC end. Prefer to show dollar caps in the OF.

maya (Sales): Procurement will push for dollar numbers, not percentages. I'll confirm the $49k. Also they want PO number on invoices and procurement approver included in the signing flow. Devin, can you be the countersigner?

devin (Legal): I can countersign. I'll prepare the redline with the 99.5% POC SLA, the credit cap, the DocuSign clause, and the conversion credit language. Uploading to the ticket by EOD.

docusign-bot: Template "Redwood POC Order Form" created (tpl_6621). Suggestion: set Auth = ID Check for customer signers if requested.

hira (Engineering): I'll add a short SLA carveout to the ticket: define availability (inference plane only), measurement (rolling 30-day), exclusions (scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, customer network issues, force majeure).

maya (Sales): Plan: Devin uploads redline, Hira posts technical carveouts, Frank will calculate dollar caps once fee confirmed, and I'll draft DocuSign routing to include procurement + legal on customer side. If procurement insists on notarization again I'll escalate. Thanks team :thumbsup:
